name: NETWORKDAYS.INTL
description: NETWORKDAYS.INTL counts the number of working days between two dates with a customizable weekend (a weekend code or a 7-character string) and optional holidays; both endpoints are included.
tldr: Counts workdays between two dates with a custom weekend.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: The first date of the period.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: The last date of the period. Both start and end dates are counted.

parameters.name: weekend
parameters.description: Optional. A number 1-7 or 11-17 selecting weekend days (1 = Sat+Sun default, 2 = Sun only, ... 7 = Fri only, 11 = Sun+Mon, ... 17 = Sat+Sun), or a 7-character string of 0/1 for Mon-Sun where 1 means weekend.

parameters.name: holidays
parameters.description: Optional range or array of dates to exclude as non-working days.

basicExample.explanation: With the default weekend (code 1, Sat+Sun), January 2024 has 23 weekdays. This matches NETWORKDAYS.

advancedExamples.title: Custom weekend (Mon and Sun off) over a week
advancedExamples.description: A 7-character string defines the off days
advancedExamples.explanation: The string "1000001" marks Monday and Sunday as weekends. In Jan 1-7, only Tue-Sat (Jan 2-6) are working, giving 5 workdays.

advancedExamples.title: Friday-Saturday weekend for a whole month
advancedExamples.scenario: A schedule where Fri and Sat are off
advancedExamples.description: The weekend string changes which days are skipped
advancedExamples.explanation: The string "0000110" marks Friday and Saturday as weekends. In January 2024, excluding the 4 Fridays and 4 Saturdays leaves 15 working days (23 minus 8).

howItWorks: NETWORKDAYS.INTL counts every day from start_date through end_date, subtracts the days marked as weekends by the weekend argument, and then subtracts any dates in the holidays list. Both endpoints are included. The weekend can be a preset code or a 7-character 0/1 string in Monday-to-Sunday order.

howToSteps.name: Enter the start and end dates
howToSteps.text: Supply the period boundaries as date serials.

howToSteps.name: Set the weekend
howToSteps.text: Use a code (1-7/11-17) or a 7-char 0/1 string (Mon-Sun).

howToSteps.name: Optionally list holidays
howToSteps.text: Pass a range or array of holiday dates.

limitations: Available only in Excel 2010 and later.
The weekend string must be exactly seven characters in Monday-to-Sunday order.
If start_date is after end_date, the result is negative.

commonErrors.cause: The weekend string is not exactly seven 0/1 characters.
commonErrors.fix: Use a valid 7-character string such as "0000011".

commonErrors.cause: An invalid weekend code (not 1-7 or 11-17) was supplied.
commonErrors.fix: Use a supported weekend code or a valid string.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: NETWORKDAYS.INTL is available in Google Sheets with identical syntax, codes, and the 7-character weekend string.

faq.question: What does the weekend string mean?
faq.answer: Seven characters for Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, where 1 marks a weekend day, e.g. "0000011" = Sat+Sun off.

faq.question: Are both endpoints counted?
faq.answer: Yes, both the start and end dates are included in the count.
